mechanicTruth: The exhaust hangs from rubber isolator loops, so when one dry-rots and splits, the pipe swings loose and knocks against the underbody only when a bump moves it - the noise shows up over bumps and goes quiet on smooth pavement, and a scrape instead of a rattle means the pipe has already dropped.

storyboardBeats.visual: Low tracking shot skimming inches above cracked asphalt, the tail end of an exhaust pipe bobbing and knocking as the car crosses a bump, dust puffing off the road, warm daylight, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.narration: Rattling under the car over every bump?

storyboardBeats.visual: Underbody on a garage lift, exhaust pipe and muffler running the length of the floor pan, a rubber hanger loop holding the pipe up, work light from below, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.motion: slow push-in toward the hanger bracket
storyboardBeats.narration: Often it is a cracked rubber exhaust hanger.

storyboardBeats.visual: Extreme macro of a rubber exhaust hanger isolator, dry rot cracks splitting the loop nearly through, rust dust caught in the split, hard raking work light, shallow depth of field, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.motion: slow orbit around the cracked loop
storyboardBeats.narration: Dry rot splits it and the pipe swings loose.

storyboardBeats.visual: Underbody wide, the exhaust pipe sagging low toward the pavement at one end, a bright scrape mark polished into the pipe seam, neutral light, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.narration: A light rattle is one clue, scraping is worse.

storyboardBeats.visual: A flashlight beam sweeping along the exhaust line from underneath a car on a lift, no one in frame, the beam picking out each hanger in turn, warm garage light, 9:16 vertical framing
storyboardBeats.motion: beam sweeps front to back, static camera
storyboardBeats.narration: Worth a look underneath before you guess.
